purpose: Records which committed art can be regenerated and which is the only copy that exists. Checked by scripts/audit-art-provenance.mjs (pnpm art:audit).

roles.master: Generated source art. Nothing derives it; deleting it loses it. Hash-pinned.
roles.master-of-record: A runtime asset that is itself the only surviving copy, because no master was ever committed. Treat it exactly like a master: never re-encode it. Hash-pinned.
roles.derived: Reproducible from a master by the recorded recipe, so it does not need to be archived.

Live light-mode backdrop, 1480x484. No master exists: no larger or earlier version appears anywhere in git history, and the art came from a generative workflow that does not reproduce deterministically from a prompt. It was re-encoded once in 0.1.19 (232470 to 228596 bytes, 39.32 dB, max pixel delta 66) for a 1.7% saving, which is the loss this pin exists to stop repeating. That pass also cleaned chroma-contaminated edge pixels in the asset, so the current bytes are the correct ones and the earlier blob must not be restored.

Superseded light-mode backdrop, 1480x484, referenced by no runtime code. Kept because it has no master either and only ever existed as this one blob, added in the initial prototype commit. 0.1.12 also chose to retain it as release history.

Live dark-mode backdrop. The shipped copy was transcoded from an intermediate JPEG rather than re-derived from the master, so it does not match the recipe: it measures 31.78 dB against the master where a direct re-derive at the same quality reaches 33.71 dB for 23 KB more. Re-deriving would remove that generation loss.
Predecessor of the WebP above. Encoder settings were not recorded, so it re-derives visually rather than byte for byte.
